reasons: The timeframe choice affects only some parts, and the screen does not make that clear.
Most of the numbers come from a helper that is not in this packet.

terms.meaning: The app's shared memory where tasks, habits and other data are kept.
A total or average combined from many records.
A grid of coloured squares where the colour shows how much happened on each day.
The time period a view covers, here weekly, monthly or yearly.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports analytics pieces and helpers
sections.what: Brings in the icons, the store, the counter, the charts, the summary card, the heatmap and the totals helper.
sections.why: Likely reason: this page is assembled from these separate pieces.

sections.name: AnalyticsView (part 1)
sections.title: Timeframe switch and habit history
sections.what: Holds the chosen timeframe and calculates totals from all the data. Combines completed habit days into one record for the yearly grid. Three buttons let the user choose weekly, monthly or yearly.
sections.why: Likely reason: totals are calculated once so the counters and charts can share the same numbers.
sections.watch_out: The timeframe is kept only while this screen is open, so it resets when the user leaves and returns.

sections.name: AnalyticsView (part 2)
sections.title: Counter tiles and chart group
sections.what: Shows six counter tiles: productivity score, focus hours, coding hours, study hours, task completion and average sleep. The productivity score follows the timeframe choice, and the chart group also receives it.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick overview at the top, with detailed charts below.
sections.watch_out: The focus, coding, study, completion and sleep counters do not change when the timeframe changes.

sections.name: AnalyticsView (part 3)
sections.title: Yearly habit grid and summary
sections.what: Shows a 365-day grid of habit activity, followed by the written summary card.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the section title describing a yearly view.
sections.watch_out: The grid does not receive the timeframe choice, so it looks the same whichever timeframe is selected.

summary: The main analytics screen that shows key totals, a timeframe switch, charts, a yearly habit grid and a written summary.
purpose: Gives one place to see how productive the user has been across tasks, habits, focus time and sleep.
why: Likely reason: several analytics pieces are combined so the user sees the full picture on one page. Reason for the three timeframe options is not stated in detail.
how: Reads all relevant data from the store and passes it to a helper that calculates totals. Keeps the chosen timeframe on screen. Shows the timeframe buttons, six counter tiles, the chart group, a 365-day habit grid built from completed habit days, and the summary card. The productivity score and the summary heading respond to the timeframe choice.
inputs: Tasks, habits, focus sessions, assignments, internships, hackathons and projects from the store. The user's timeframe choice.
outputs: A page of counters, charts, a heatmap and a summary. No data is saved here.
risks: Most counters and charts do not change with the timeframe, which may mislead a user who expects them to. All totals depend on the helper function being correct. Each completed habit on a day adds to that day's count, so busy days look brighter.
debug: If totals look wrong, check calculateAggregateAnalytics in the analyticsHelpers file. If the habit grid is empty, check that habit history records use the completed status. If the timeframe buttons seem to do nothing, check the child components, since most of them ignore it.
